done_when: When two rounds in a row leave the same failing test or finding, or the change grows past its size limit, Forge stops the item and prints a ready-to-ask question naming the item, what is stuck and what the worker tried, with the choices: switch this item to the other tool, keep the same tool for one more round, or narrow or split; the owner's choice is recorded and the next round follows it

findings.body: Raise: Not done. `stuck_round` increments the failure count on every `forge work` call, using the failing test output retained by the last `forge close`. If an agent runs `forge work` twice before closing again, the second call stops the item using the same test result even though the intervening worker round has not been tested. The command-level tests always run close between work calls, so they miss this normal rerun path.
findings.title: Not done: one failed close can be counted as two stuck rounds

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The question derives “The worker tried” solely from commit subjects and falls back to “no new commits.” A worker can attempt to fix a failing test, finish without a commit, and leave the test failing on the next close. Forge then asks the owner without saying what that worker tried, despite that being a required part of the question. The named proof uses a worker that commits “Worker round,” so it does not cover this stuck case.
findings.title: Not done: a worker with no commit leaves no account of what it tried

stop.reason: Coordinator decision under the owner's bar: finding 1 (false re-count) is fixed at the current head; findings 2 (Jest tail key, Gain 2 Work 2 Harm 1) and 3 (refusal hint, Gain 2 Work 1 Harm 1) are recorded as lived-with

why: When a worker can't fix a problem or keeps making the change bigger, Forge sends it back round after round and nobody is told
